name: Nekoda
overview: Nekoda was a male member of the tribe of Levi, serving as a temple servant. His role was connected to the religious duties associated with the temple, reflecting the Levitical responsibility for worship and service. Scripture mentions him specifically in the context of the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Nekoda appears in Scripture without a provided meaning or special title. It is simply recorded as a proper name in Ezra 2:48, with no indication that it was given by God or carries a particular theological significance.
familyAndRelationships: Nekoda is identified as a descendant of Levi, indicating his Levitical heritage. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not record any further family relationships or connections for Nekoda.
scriptureSignificance: Nekoda's significance lies in his role as a temple servant within the Levitical tribe during the restoration period after the exile. His mention in Ezra 2:48 highlights the reestablishment of temple service and the faithful continuation of Levitical duties under God's providence. This underscores the importance of faithful service in the worship of the Lord and the preservation of His covenant community.
